FOREWORD This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards, after the draft by the Nutrition Sectional Committee had been approved by the Food and Agriculture Council. Ready Upma the country. edible oils or roasted nuts, The process quantity of convenience potential for finalized Division

is a very popular breakfast item in South India and is gaining popularity throughout It is traditionally prepared by roasting wheat Semolina and adding to it suitable fat, salt, spices, roasted Dais and water and cooking it. Fried raisins and fried/ such as cashewnuts, etc, also added to improve taste. of making Upma using water, adding the mix it provides the ready use by Defence for pack the ready mix, involves bringing to boil the appropriate to it and lightly heating. Due to ease in cooking, and mix is gradually gaining popularity. It also has great ration and in various expeditions. by dry blending of the roasted/cooked dried Semolina, seeds, salt and other Dais, edible fats or oils, mustard

Ready Upma mix may be prepared dehydrated vegetables, roasted/fried optional ingredients.

Some ready mixes contain large amounts of fats. To ensure that ihese do not get rancid during sto'rage, the committee considered it necessary to lay down the maximum Iimit of alcoholic acidity of extracted fat. At present data on this characteristics is not available. However, investigations on this part are currently being carried out in various laboratories, and on availability of data, an amendment incorporating this limit will be issued to the standard. In the formulation restrictions of this standard, due consideration has been given to the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 and the Rules framed thereunder and the Standards of Weights and the standard is subject to the Measures ( Packaged Commodities ) Rules, 1977. However, imposed under these wherever applicable. For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or caIculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordance with IS 2 : 1960 `Rules for rounding off numerical values ( revised )`. The number of significant pIaces retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

1 SCOPE This standard prescribes the requirements and methods of sampling and test for ready Upma mix. 2 REFERENCES The Indian Standard listed in Annex necessary adjuncts to this standard. 3 TERMINOLOGY
Upma For the purpose of this standard, ready _1 mix shall mean a mix contammg roasred/precookodfdried wheat semolina, edible fat or oil ( see 4.1.2 ), salt, dried and fried vegetables, roasted/fried Dais, mustard seeds with or without ingredients given in 4.2 and prepared by dry blen.ding of the various ingredients.

1980 ). 5 REQUIREMENTS 5.1 Description 5.1.1 The ready Upma mix shall have a uniform distribution of various ingredients. It shall be a slightly brownish-white or amber colour. It should have a characteristic flavour of roasted Semolina and added spices and shall be free from burnt or charred particles. The product shall be free from any unpleasant rancid or any other undesirable stored odour. The dry vegetables shall have a characteristic colour, taste and flavour of fresh vegetables and shall not have undergone browning and dis-colouration or excessive shrinkage. The material shall be free from any signs of insects or fungus infestation or microbial deterioration. The mix shall be free from synthetic colouring matter. 5.1.2 When water for 6 into freshly and flavour the ready Upma mix is boiled with minutes, it shall be reconstituted prepared Upma, free from textural defects.

The ready Upma mix shall be packed in flexible thermoplastic, food grade films or multilayer or monolayer construction, or their laminate with paper and/or aluminium foil so as to provide a high resistance to the passage of oxygen and water vapour and to produce an effective heat seal. The sealing shall be done hermetically with or without nitrogen flushing to retain the contents in a fresh condition. The mix may also be packed in other conventional suitable rigid containers such as tin, HDPE, glass, etc. 6.1.1 The material may preferably be packed in 100 g, 200 g, 400 g, 500 g, or 1 000 g packs or in sizes as agreed to between the purchaser and the vendor. 6.2 Marking

DETERMINATION B-l APPARATUS B-l.1 Soxhlet Extraction Apparatus B-2 SOLVENT B-2.1 Ethyl Ether, or distilling below 65�C. B-3 PROCEDURE Transfer about 10 g of the material, accurately weighed, to a suitable thimble and extract with the solvent in a Soxhlet extraction apparatus for about 16 hours. Dry the extract contained in the Soxhlet flask, whose empty mass has previously been determined, after taring at 95 to 1OOoCfor 30 minutes. Cool in a desiccator and. weigh. Continue drying and weighing alternatively at 30 minute intervals until the Petroleum Ether OF FAT

loss in mass between two successive weighings is not more than one milligram. Record the lowest mass.

Standard

Mark

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Br~eau Q/" Ztuliurl Stmtlurtls Act, lY86 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by RIS and operated by the producer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from the Bureau of Indian Standards.
